riskLevels.name: Limited
riskLevels.description: Low-impact software with limited state, exposure, and failure radius.

riskLevels.name: Standard
riskLevels.description: Normal user-facing or business software with recoverable operational impact.

riskLevels.name: High
riskLevels.description: Software with sensitive data, privileged effects, material transactions, or important availability obligations.

riskLevels.name: Critical
riskLevels.description: Safety-relevant, regulated, infrastructure-control, or organization-critical software with severe failure consequences.

controlFamilies.name: Governance
controlFamilies.description: Ownership, authority, risk, applicability, and exceptions.

controlFamilies.name: Requirements
controlFamilies.description: Problem definition, scope, constraints, acceptance, and traceability.

controlFamilies.name: Architecture
controlFamilies.description: Boundaries, interfaces, state, dependencies, failure behavior, and decisions.

controlFamilies.name: Version control
controlFamilies.description: Isolation, commits, review, integration, and immutable history.

controlFamilies.name: Quality
controlFamilies.description: Risk-based verification, regression, compatibility, performance, and recovery.

controlFamilies.name: Security and privacy
controlFamilies.description: Threat boundaries, identity, access, inputs, secrets, privacy, and response.

controlFamilies.name: Supply chain
controlFamilies.description: Dependency identity, integrity, provenance, licensing, vulnerability, and build evidence.

controlFamilies.name: Data and state
controlFamilies.description: Ownership, identity, validation, migration, retention, backup, export, and deletion.

controlFamilies.name: Release

controlFamilies.name: Documentation
controlFamilies.description: Required knowledge, evidence quality, freshness, consistency, and handoff.

controls.title: Accountable owner
controls.requirement: The project MUST identify an accountable owner with authority over scope, risk acceptance, release, and retirement.

controls.title: Purpose and consumers
controls.requirement: The project MUST record its purpose, intended consumers, supported use, and explicitly excluded use.

controls.title: Owner control and portability
controls.requirement: The owner MUST retain effective access to source, history, configuration, credentials, data, build instructions, release artifacts, and recovery material required to continue or migrate the project.

controls.title: Risk classification
controls.requirement: The project MUST select and justify one current risk level from R1 through R4 and MUST reassess it after material scope or exposure changes.

controls.title: Control applicability
controls.requirement: Every control MUST have a recorded applicability decision with specific rationale and evidence; blanket exclusions are prohibited.

controls.title: Explicit approval
controls.requirement: Implementation, release, production admission, risk acceptance, and retirement decisions MUST be approved by the authority declared in the project profile.

controls.title: Time-bounded exceptions
controls.requirement: Any exception MUST identify the affected control, scope, owner approval, risk, start date, expiry date, and remediation plan and MUST NOT be treated as a pass.

controls.title: Problem statement
controls.requirement: Each change MUST state the problem or opportunity in terms that can be evaluated independently of the proposed implementation.

controls.title: Defined scope
controls.requirement: Each change MUST define included behavior, excluded behavior, affected consumers, and affected project boundaries.

controls.title: Measurable acceptance
controls.requirement: Requirements MUST include observable acceptance criteria that identify the evidence needed to prove completion.

controls.title: Constraints and assumptions
controls.requirement: Material technical, legal, operational, schedule, compatibility, and ownership constraints and assumptions MUST be recorded and validated.

controls.title: Requirement traceability
controls.requirement: Every accepted requirement MUST be traceable to design, implementation, verification, review, and release evidence or to an approved non-applicability decision.

controls.title: Scope-change control
controls.requirement: A material change to scope, assumptions, risk, or acceptance criteria MUST be explicitly reviewed and approved before dependent work continues.

controls.title: System context and boundaries
controls.requirement: The project MUST document its boundary, consumers, external systems, trust boundaries, and ownership boundaries at a level proportionate to risk.

controls.title: Component responsibilities
controls.requirement: Components MUST have understandable responsibilities, dependencies, and change boundaries so behavior can be reasoned about and reviewed.

controls.title: Explicit interfaces
controls.requirement: Interfaces between components and with consumers MUST define inputs, outputs, errors, compatibility expectations, and ownership.

controls.title: State ownership
controls.requirement: State ownership, consistency, lifecycle, and authority MUST be explicit wherever the project creates, reads, changes, or deletes state.

controls.title: Failure behavior
controls.requirement: Material failure modes, partial-failure behavior, limits, retries, timeouts, recovery, and fail-open or fail-closed decisions MUST be designed explicitly.

controls.title: Dependency replacement
controls.requirement: Material external dependencies MUST have documented boundaries, configuration ownership, and a feasible upgrade, replacement, disablement, or exit path.

controls.title: Architecture decisions
controls.requirement: Long-lived or difficult-to-reverse architecture decisions SHOULD record considered alternatives, consequences, and the approval decision.

controls.title: Version-controlled source
controls.requirement: Source, configuration, schemas, migrations, build instructions, tests, and governance artifacts required to reproduce a release MUST be version controlled unless an approved exclusion explains the alternative authority.

controls.title: Isolated change branch
controls.requirement: Each change MUST use an isolated branch or equivalent workspace based on the project's current protected default branch or an explicitly approved equivalent. A safe existing branch or workspace MAY be reused for a continuing task when ownership, base reference, and dirty state are recorded and preserved; it MUST NOT overwrite unrelated work.

controls.title: Focused commits
controls.requirement: Commits MUST be reviewable, accurately described, limited to intentional scope, and free of unrelated owner work or secrets.

controls.title: Recorded change review
controls.requirement: Every integrated change MUST have a PR, MR, or equivalent durable review object that records scope, exactly one canonical change type, exactly one R1-R4 risk classification with rationale, optional controlled flags, evidence, findings, and disposition.

controls.title: Truthful checks
controls.requirement: Automated and manual check results MUST distinguish executed passes, failures, omissions, blockers, historical evidence, and discovery-only results.

controls.title: Explicit integration history
controls.requirement: Integration into the protected default branch MUST preserve an explicit integration record and the detailed commits required for traceability.

controls.title: Immutable published history
controls.requirement: Published commits, release references, review records, and audit evidence MUST NOT be silently rewritten, moved, or deleted.

controls.title: Risk-based verification matrix
controls.requirement: The project MUST define a verification matrix that maps relevant behaviors and risks to test or review evidence and states why omitted categories are not applicable.

controls.title: Acceptance verification
controls.requirement: Every acceptance criterion MUST have current evidence at the same scope and environment required by the criterion.

controls.title: Regression protection
controls.requirement: A defect fix or behavior change MUST include repeatable evidence capable of detecting recurrence unless the project profile approves a stronger alternative.

controls.title: Static validation
controls.requirement: Applicable source, configuration, schema, and artifact formats MUST be validated with deterministic static checks.

controls.title: Component behavior
controls.requirement: Material component behavior and error handling MUST be verified at the smallest useful boundary.

controls.title: Integration boundaries
controls.requirement: Material interactions across owned or external boundaries MUST be verified using representative interfaces, state, and failure behavior.

controls.title: Consumer workflows
controls.requirement: Critical consumer workflows MUST be verified end to end at a representative level or have an approved reason and alternative evidence.

controls.title: Compatibility
controls.requirement: Supported platforms, environments, versions, interfaces, and upgrade paths MUST have a declared compatibility policy and representative evidence.

controls.title: Installation and migration
controls.requirement: Applicable clean installation, repeat installation, upgrade, migration, and rollback paths MUST be verified without assuming an existing healthy state.

controls.title: Resource and performance limits
controls.requirement: Material latency, throughput, capacity, resource, size, and concurrency limits MUST be defined and verified where exceeding them can affect consumers or safety.

controls.title: Human interaction quality
controls.requirement: Projects with human interaction MUST verify applicable accessibility, usability, input, error, and recovery behavior; projects without human interaction MUST record non-applicability.

controls.title: Recovery verification
controls.requirement: Where failure can lose state or interrupt required service, recovery procedures MUST be exercised and verified rather than documented only.

controls.title: Threat and trust model
controls.requirement: The project MUST identify protected assets, actors, entry points, trust boundaries, abuse cases, and security assumptions proportionate to risk.

controls.title: Identity and authorization
controls.requirement: Identity, authentication, authorization, session, and privileged-action controls MUST be explicit, least-privileged, and verified wherever access distinctions exist.

controls.title: Input and output safety
controls.requirement: Untrusted input MUST be bounded and validated, and output MUST be encoded or constrained for its destination context.

controls.title: Secure state changes
controls.requirement: State-changing actions MUST verify authority, target, integrity, replay protection where relevant, and safe failure behavior.

controls.title: Secret management
controls.requirement: Secrets MUST be excluded from source and artifacts, stored through an approved mechanism, minimally scoped, rotated when required, and prevented from unsafe logs or error output.

controls.title: External communication
controls.requirement: External communication MUST define approved destinations, transport protection, authentication, timeouts, size limits, data handling, and failure policy.

controls.title: Sensitive-data classification
controls.requirement: The project MUST classify data it receives, creates, infers, stores, transmits, logs, or exposes and apply controls appropriate to sensitivity and obligations.

controls.title: Privacy obligations
controls.requirement: Where personal or sensitive data exists, collection, purpose, minimization, access, retention, transfer, deletion, and disclosure obligations MUST be documented and verified.

controls.title: Safe files and execution
controls.requirement: File access, parsing, upload, extraction, execution, and generated paths MUST enforce containment, type, size, integrity, permission, and unsafe-link boundaries where applicable.

controls.title: Secure defaults and failure
controls.requirement: Security-relevant defaults MUST minimize exposure, and missing or unverifiable security state MUST fail closed unless an approved design proves fail-open behavior is safer.

controls.title: Security findings
controls.requirement: Security findings MUST record severity, affected version, evidence, disposition, owner, and remediation or approved exception; tool coverage limits MUST remain explicit.

controls.title: Incident readiness
controls.requirement: Projects with material security or availability impact MUST define detection, containment, evidence preservation, communication, recovery, and post-incident review responsibilities.

controls.title: Third-party inventory
controls.requirement: Every third-party code, service, model, asset, tool, and runtime required to build, test, deliver, or operate the project MUST have an owned inventory or a justified exclusion.

controls.title: Exact identity and integrity
controls.requirement: Third-party components and release-critical tools MUST be identified by exact version or immutable reference and verified by integrity or provenance evidence.

controls.title: Authoritative provenance
controls.requirement: Third-party material MUST come from a recorded authoritative source or an approved mirrored source whose correspondence is verified.

controls.title: License decision
controls.requirement: Each third-party component MUST have a verified license and a documented decision covering intended use, modification, distribution, disclosure, attribution, and commercial constraints.

controls.title: Vulnerability evidence
controls.requirement: Applicable dependencies, runtimes, images, and artifacts MUST have current vulnerability evidence that identifies coverage limits and affected exact versions.

controls.title: Controlled updates
controls.requirement: Dependency and tool updates MUST be reviewed, verified, and intentionally adopted; production execution MUST NOT silently acquire unreviewed versions.

controls.title: Build provenance
controls.requirement: Release artifacts MUST be traceable to source, build instructions, inputs, tool identities, and the environment or service that produced them.

controls.title: Dependency minimization
controls.requirement: The project SHOULD avoid unnecessary third-party components and SHOULD record the value and replacement strategy for material dependencies.

controls.title: Authoritative state
controls.requirement: For every material state domain, the project MUST identify the authoritative source, writer ownership, identity model, and consistency expectations.

controls.title: Schema and format
controls.requirement: Persistent or exchanged data MUST have versioned, validated formats or schemas and defined compatibility behavior.

controls.title: Stable identity
controls.requirement: Material entities and records MUST use stable identities appropriate to their lifecycle rather than mutable display values.

controls.title: Validated writes
controls.requirement: Data changes MUST validate complete intended input before irreversible writes and MUST define atomicity, idempotency, retry, and partial-failure behavior.

controls.title: Migration and rollback
controls.requirement: Data-format or state transitions MUST have versioned migration, compatibility, validation, and rollback or recovery procedures.

controls.title: Retention and deletion
controls.requirement: Retained state MUST have explicit retention, archival, legal-hold where applicable, deletion, and verification rules.

controls.title: Export and portability
controls.requirement: Owner-controlled data and material configuration MUST have a documented, usable export path in a sufficiently described format.

controls.title: Backup and restoration
controls.requirement: Where state loss is material, backups MUST define scope, protection, integrity, retention, separation, recovery objectives, and successful restoration evidence.

controls.title: Unique version
controls.requirement: Every release MUST have a unique, monotonically progressing version under a documented versioning policy; published versions MUST NOT be reused.

controls.title: Change record
controls.requirement: Every release MUST have a human-readable change record describing material additions, changes, fixes, removals, security impact, compatibility, and actual verification state.

controls.title: Immutable source reference
controls.requirement: Every release MUST have an immutable source reference that resolves to the intended integrated source state. The project's release reference MUST define whether that reference is an annotated tag or another integrity-protected native release reference.

controls.title: Release record
controls.requirement: Every immutable release reference MUST have a durable release record containing version, scope, verification, security state, compatibility, upgrade, and rollback information.

controls.title: Artifact correspondence
controls.requirement: Distributed artifacts and source archives MUST be verified to correspond to the immutable source reference, declared version, and recorded build inputs.

controls.title: Release gate
controls.requirement: A release MUST NOT proceed while an applicable mandatory control is FAIL, NOT_RUN, BLOCKED, PRIOR_PASS, or DISCOVERED, or while required evidence is missing, stale, or contradictory.

controls.title: Upgrade and rollback
controls.requirement: A release MUST describe required upgrade, migration, compatibility, and rollback or recovery actions at a level appropriate to its impact.

controls.title: Milestone traceability
controls.requirement: The version, change record, review object, integrated commits, immutable reference, release record, and artifacts MUST be mutually traceable.

controls.title: Truthful readiness state
controls.requirement: Development-ready, releasable, deliverable, production-ready, and retired states MUST be reported separately and MUST reflect the strictest unresolved applicable gate.

controls.title: Delivery model
controls.requirement: The project MUST define how supported consumers obtain, configure, update, verify, and remove or retire the software.

controls.title: Environment ownership
controls.requirement: Supported environments, configuration authority, credentials, external services, and differences between development, verification, and operational use MUST be documented.

controls.title: Observability
controls.requirement: Where ongoing operation matters, the project MUST define health, logging, metrics, tracing, alerting, evidence retention, and sensitive-data boundaries proportionate to risk.

controls.title: Operational limits
controls.requirement: Operational capacity, quotas, dependencies, maintenance, degraded behavior, and stop conditions MUST be known where they can affect supported use.

controls.title: Continuity and recovery
controls.requirement: Projects with continuity obligations MUST define recovery objectives, responsibilities, dependencies, procedures, communication, and exercised restoration evidence.

controls.title: Support and maintenance
controls.requirement: The project MUST define supported versions, issue intake, severity, response ownership, update policy, and end-of-support behavior appropriate to its distribution model.

controls.title: Operational change safety
controls.requirement: Operationally material changes MUST have controlled rollout, validation, stop, rollback or recovery, and communication procedures proportionate to risk.

controls.title: Retirement
controls.requirement: Retirement MUST address consumer notice, migration or export, access revocation, dependency shutdown, retention, secure deletion, evidence preservation, and ownership transfer or archive.

controls.title: Project entry point
controls.requirement: The project MUST provide an authoritative entry point describing purpose, ownership, setup, supported use, verification, delivery, and where deeper records are maintained.

controls.title: Reproducible instructions
controls.requirement: Build, verification, delivery, upgrade, backup, restoration, and retirement instructions MUST be exact, current, and executable for each applicable project lifecycle stage.

controls.title: Evidence provenance
controls.requirement: Evidence MUST identify the subject version, command or method, environment, time, result, coverage, limitations, and immutable or integrity-protected location.

controls.title: Evidence freshness
controls.requirement: Evidence MUST be current for the version and gate it supports; historical or discovery-only results MUST remain visibly distinct from current execution.

controls.title: Consistency
controls.requirement: Versions, scope, controls, readiness, findings, commands, paths, links, and artifact identities MUST be internally consistent across human and machine records.

controls.title: No unsupported claims
controls.requirement: Documentation and reports MUST NOT claim execution, coverage, safety, compliance, readiness, or completion beyond the exact evidence available.

controls.title: Knowledge transfer
controls.requirement: Material project knowledge required to continue, verify, recover, migrate, support, or retire the project MUST be recorded outside a single person's memory.

controls.title: Decision history
controls.requirement: Material requirement, design, risk, exception, and release decisions SHOULD retain rationale, alternatives, approver, and consequences.
